findings.excerpt: pullback H f b a = f (b * φ a)
findings.problem: This is the only evaluation rule for the `pullback` abbreviation, and it is not a simp lemma. The underlying `pullback_monoidHom_def` is not simp either. Every proof that needs to evaluate `pullback` has to name it by hand (`simp [pullback_def, ha, mul_assoc]` at line 70, `simp [this, pullback_def]` at line 88, `simp [pullback_def, mul_assoc]` at line 213, and `simp only [pushforward_apply_apply, pullback_def, ...]` at line 262). The left side is an application of a bundled-map coercion to a structure-valued abbrev, which the simp set cannot unfold to the underlying function. The right side `f (b * φ a)` is the canonical form, and it is strictly simpler, so the rewrite has no loop risk.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `pullback_def` (and, if desired, `pullback_monoidHom_def` in CompactlySupported.lean) with `@[to_additive (attr := simp)]`. Then drop the explicit `pullback_def` from the `simp` calls at lines 70, 88 and 213, keeping it in the `simp only` at line 262 unless that call is also replaced. Because `pullback` is `abbrev`, the discrimination-tree key should be the reducible unfolding, so check that the lemma fires on `H.pullback f b a`. This has not been compiled.
findings.benefit: Downstream users who work with `pullback` get `f (b * φ a)` from plain `simp`, with no need to know the lemma name. The four call sites in this file become simpler, and the normal form is the same everywhere.
